title: Points of algebraic stacks, stabilisers and residual gerbes
summary: Monomorphisms, immersions, closed substacks and reductions of algebraic stacks; finite type points and automorphism group spaces; gerbes of algebraic stacks and the dense open gerbe; reduced one-point stacks and residual gerbes with their characterisation, uniqueness, regularity, functoriality and existence (finite type points, flat quasi-finite presentations, gerbes, quasi-compact inertia, locally Noetherian stacks); decent stacks, residue fields, algebraicity of points with quasi-compact diagonal and the fppf image of a representative; residual gerbes at representatives and BG_x at rational points; infinitesimal neighbourhoods, the normal space and the exact sequence 0 -> T_{BG_x} -> T_{X,x} -> N_x -> 0.

targets.name: Stacks.HasSmoothLocalProperty
targets.statement: For a property P of schemes local in the smooth topology, an algebraic stack has P iff some scheme with a smooth surjective morphism to it has P; equivalently every scheme or algebraic space smooth over it has P. Instances: reduced, regular, locally Noetherian.
hypotheses: P local in the smooth topology on schemes

api.name: atlas_independent
api.statement: If one smooth surjective scheme atlas has P, every scheme smooth over X has P.

api.name: of_smooth
api.statement: P passes along smooth morphisms Y -> X and descends along smooth surjective ones.

api.name: locallyNoetherian_iff
api.statement: For P locally Noetherian the notion is SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20's locally Noetherian stack; for schemes it is Mathlib IsReduced / IsLocallyNoetherian and §4.13 IsRegular.

api.name: regular_reduced
api.statement: A regular algebraic stack is reduced and locally Noetherian.

api.name: open
api.statement: Open substacks inherit P.

tests.name: dualNumberQuotient_notReduced

targets.name: Stacks.IsMonomorphism
targets.statement: A morphism of algebraic stacks is a monomorphism if it is representable by algebraic spaces with monomorphic base changes; equivalently fully faithful, equivalently its diagonal is an equivalence, equivalently after one surjective flat lfp base change from an algebraic space it is a monomorphism of algebraic spaces. A monomorphism from a nonempty algebraic space to Spec k is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: f : X -> Y a morphism of algebraic stacks
rigidity: T a nonempty algebraic space, T -> Spec k a monomorphism, k a field

locator.where: Definition 100.8.1, Lemmas 100.8.2-100.8.6, lines 707-762; Morphisms of Spaces Lemma 67.10.8 used at stacks-06ML line 1204; stacks-06RD lines 445-451 and 591-608 (Lemmas 101.4.15, 101.5.6)

api.name: baseChange
api.statement: Monomorphisms are stable under base change and composition; equivalences are monomorphisms.

api.name: injective_points
api.statement: |f| is injective for a monomorphism f.

api.name: diagonal_cartesian
api.statement: For X -> X' -> Y with X -> X' mono, the diagonal square is 2-cartesian.

api.name: inertia
api.statement: I_X = I_Y x_Y X for a monomorphism; hence G_x = G_{f x}.

api.name: separated_DM
api.statement: A monomorphism is separated and DM.

tests.name: pointToBG_notMono
tests.statement: Spec k -> BG for G nontrivial is not a monomorphism since Spec k x_BG Spec k = G.

tests.name: C_over_R
tests.statement: Spec C -> Spec R is injective on points but not a monomorphism.

tests.name: rigidity_needs_field
tests.statement: Spec k -> Spec k[eps] is a nonempty monomorphism and not an isomorphism.

tests.name: example_100_11_6
tests.statement: For U = Spec(Qbar ⊗_Q Qbar) and G = Gal(Qbar/Q) discrete acting through the second factor, X = U/G lies over Spec Qbar; the point Spec Qbar -> U -> X is a section of X -> Spec Qbar, hence a monomorphism between one-point spaces, and not an isomorphism (U x_X Spec Qbar = G x Spec Qbar is discrete); there is no morphism Spec Q -> X.

targets.name: Stacks.IsImmersion
targets.statement: Open immersions, closed immersions and immersions of algebraic stacks are morphisms representable by algebraic spaces with the corresponding property; open, closed and locally closed substacks are strictly full algebraic substacks with such inclusions. They are stable under base change and composition, fppf local on the target, monomorphisms, homeomorphisms onto locally closed subsets; immersions factor uniquely through a locally closed substack; on a presentation [U/R] locally closed substacks are R-invariant locally closed subspaces of U; open substacks are open subsets of |X|.
hypotheses: presentation statements: [U/R] -> X a smooth presentation

api.name: baseChange_comp
api.statement: Immersions are stable under base change and composition and fppf local on the target.

api.name: isMonomorphism
api.statement: An immersion is a monomorphism and |i| is a homeomorphism onto a locally closed subset.

api.name: factor_substack
api.statement: Every immersion factors uniquely as an equivalence onto a locally closed substack followed by the inclusion.

api.name: presentationEquiv
api.statement: For X = [U/R], Z |-> U x_X Z is a bijection to R-invariant locally closed subspaces; factorisation is tested on U.

api.name: opensEquiv
api.statement: Open substacks correspond to open subsets of |X|, compatibly with SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.7 opensEquiv.

tests.name: BGm_closed
tests.statement: B G_m = [{0}/G_m] -> [A^1/G_m] is a closed immersion with open complement Spec k.

tests.name: genericPoint_notImmersion
tests.statement: Spec k(t) -> A^1_k is a monomorphism and not an immersion.

tests.name: uniqueness_is_equality
tests.statement: For Spec k ⊔ Spec k the two copies are equivalent but distinct open substacks.

tests.name: space_opens
tests.statement: For an algebraic space the open substacks are §1.7's open subspaces.

targets.name: Stacks.infinitesimalNeighbourhood
targets.statement: Closed substacks of X correspond bijectively and inclusion-reversingly to quasi-coherent ideals of O_X; V(I) x_X Y = V(I O_Y) for every Y -> X. The n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of a closed substack Z with ideal I is V(I^{n+1}).
hypotheses: I a quasi-coherent ideal in SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.22's Stacks.QCoh X

locator.where: Lemma 100.9.11, lines 872-888, with stacks-sheaves-on-stacks lines 953-955 (Proposition 96.14.3) and ahr2020 lines 248-252 (§1.5)

api.name: closedSubstackEquivIdeal
api.statement: Z |-> ker(O_X -> i_* O_Z) and I |-> V(I) are inverse bijections.

api.name: factor_iff
api.statement: x : T -> X factors through V(I) iff the image of x^* I -> O_T is zero.

api.name: neighbourhood_chain
api.statement: X^[0]_Z = Z and X^[n] -> X^[n+1] are first-order thickenings with the same points.

api.name: neighbourhood_baseChange
api.statement: X^[n]_Z x_X Y = Y^[n]_{Z x_X Y} for every Y -> X.

tests.name: A1_origin
tests.statement: For A^1_k and the origin, X^[n] = Spec k[t]/(t^{n+1}) of length n+1.

tests.name: dualNumbers
tests.statement: For Spec k[eps] and its reduced point, X^[n] = X for n >= 1 and X^[0] = Spec k.

tests.name: BGm_neighbourhood
tests.statement: For B G_m in [A^1/G_m], X^[n] = [Spec k[t]/(t^{n+1}) / G_m].

tests.name: ideal_not_radical
tests.statement: The ideal of V((t^2)) is (t^2), not (t); a support-only correspondence fails.

targets.name: Stacks.reducedInduced
targets.statement: For a closed subset T of |X| there is a unique reduced closed substack with points T; this is the reduced induced closed substack, X_red is the case T = |X|, and locally closed subsets get reduced induced locally closed substacks. A morphism from a reduced stack factors through a closed substack iff its image lies in it.
hypotheses: T a closed (or locally closed) subset of |X|

locator.where: Lemmas 100.10.1-100.10.3, Definition 100.10.4, Remark 100.10.5, lines 1073-1125; stacks-06RD lines 1484-1500

api.name: eq_of_reduced
api.statement: A closed substack of a reduced X with all points of X is X.

api.name: factor_iff_image
api.statement: For Y reduced, Y -> X factors through closed Z iff |f|(|Y|) ⊆ |Z|.

api.name: reduction
api.statement: X_red -> X is a closed immersion and a homeomorphism on points.

api.name: locallyNoetherian
api.statement: Locally closed substacks of locally Noetherian stacks are locally Noetherian.

api.name: scheme_case
api.statement: For a scheme it is the closed subscheme of Mathlib's vanishingIdeal.

tests.name: dualNumber_red
tests.statement: (Spec k[eps])_red = Spec k and [Spec k[t]/(t^2)/G_m]_red = B G_m.

tests.name: uniqueness_needs_reduced
tests.statement: Spec k and Spec k[t]/(t^2) in A^1 share support {0}; only the first is reduced.

tests.name: factor_needs_reduced
tests.statement: Spec k[eps] -> A^1, t |-> eps, does not factor through the reduced origin.

tests.name: A1Gm_points
tests.statement: On [A^1/G_m] the reduced induced substacks on 0 and 1 are B G_m and Spec k.

layers.title: Points of finite type and automorphism groups

targets.name: Stacks.IsFiniteTypePoint
targets.statement: A point of |X| is a finite type point if some representative Spec k -> X is locally of finite type; equivalently it is the image of a closed point of a scheme smooth over X. Locally finite type morphisms preserve finite type points (surjectively if surjective), and finite type points are dense in every closed subset.

api.name: iff_closedPoint
api.statement: x is finite type iff x = phi(u) for a smooth phi : U -> X and a closed point u of a scheme U.

api.name: map
api.statement: Locally finite type f maps finite type points to finite type points, onto them if f is surjective.

api.name: dense
api.statement: Every nonempty locally closed subset of |X| contains a finite type point.

tests.name: Zp_generic
tests.statement: The generic point of Spec Z_(p) is a finite type point and not closed.

tests.name: A1Gm_open
tests.statement: The open point 1 of [A^1/G_m] is a finite type point and not closed.

tests.name: A1_generic_not
tests.statement: The generic point of A^1_k is not a finite type point though Spec k(t) -> A^1 is flat.

tests.name: scheme_closed
tests.statement: For schemes locally of finite type over a field, finite type points are closed points (Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace).

targets.name: Stacks.pointOfObject
targets.statement: Every closed point of |X| is a finite type point. For a field k the map from isomorphism classes of objects of X over Spec k to |X| is natural and compatible with field extension; a point is in its image iff it has a representative over k.

locator.where: Definition 100.4.2 and the discussion after it, lines 399-423; stacks-06RD lines 1593-1601 (Lemma 101.18.6)

api.name: natural
api.statement: The map is natural in X and compatible with pullback along field extensions.

api.name: image_iff
api.statement: A point is in the image iff it has a representative over k.

api.name: fibre
api.statement: Two objects over k have the same image iff they become isomorphic over an extension.

tests.name: BZ2_R
tests.statement: For B(Z/2) over R the two real torsors map to the one point: not injective.

tests.name: A1_R
tests.statement: For A^1_R the point t^2+1 = 0 is not in the image: not surjective.

tests.name: absolute_vs_relative
tests.statement: k-morphisms Spec k -> X for X locally finite type over algebraically closed k biject onto closed points, while an embedding C(t) -> C gives Spec C -> A^1_C onto the generic point.

targets.name: Stacks.automorphismGroupSpace
targets.statement: For x : Spec k -> X, G_x = Isom(x,x) = Spec k x_X I_X is a group algebraic space over k, compatible with field extension; properties invariant under field extension depend only on the point; isomorphism of G_x -> G_{f x} depends only on the point; for a presentation G_x is the groupoid stabilizer at a lift.
hypotheses: x : Spec k -> X with k a field

api.name: baseChange
api.statement: G_{x'} = G_x x_k k' for k ⊆ k'.

api.name: pointProperty
api.statement: For P invariant under field extension, G_x has P for one representative iff for all.

api.name: isoOnAutomorphismGroups
api.statement: f induces an isomorphism of automorphism groups at x iff G_x -> G_{f x} is an isomorphism for one, equivalently every, representative.

api.name: stabilizerAt
api.statement: For [U/R] -> X and u over x, G_x is SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.14's stabilizerAt u.

api.name: isomPseudoTorsor
api.statement: Isom(x1,x2) is a pseudo-torsor under Isom(x2,x2).

tests.name: BG_trivial
tests.statement: G_x = G at the trivial torsor of BG; G_x trivial on algebraic spaces.

tests.name: A1Gm
tests.statement: On [A^1/G_m], G_0 = G_m and G_1 = 1.

tests.name: Bmup_points
tests.statement: On B mu_p over F_p, G_x = mu_p is nonreduced with trivial Fbar_p-points; a points-based definition sees nothing.

tests.name: kPoints_not_invariant
tests.statement: On B(mu_3) over Q, mu_3(Q) = 1 but mu_3(Q(zeta_3)) = Z/3: not a property of the point.

targets.name: Stacks.automorphismGroupSpace_isScheme
targets.statement: G_x is a scheme if the diagonal of X is quasi-separated or locally separated, or X is quasi-DM, or I_X -> X is quasi-separated, locally separated or locally quasi-finite.
hypotheses: one of the six listed conditions

tests.name: nonseparated_group
tests.statement: For G = A^1_k/Z (characteristic zero) BG has G_x = G, not a scheme; inertia not quasi-separated.

tests.name: DM_etale_notFinite
tests.statement: On a Deligne-Mumford stack G_x is an etale group scheme (unramified inertia), finite when I_X -> X is quasi-compact; BZ over k is DM with G_x = Z_k etale and not finite, B(Z/2) has G_x = (Z/2)_k finite etale.

tests.name: BGm
tests.statement: B G_m has affine diagonal and G_x = G_m is a scheme though B G_m is not quasi-DM.

targets.name: Stacks.IsGerbeOver
targets.statement: A morphism of algebraic stacks makes X a gerbe over Y when AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry §4.1's relativeGerbe holds on the fppf site; X is a gerbe if it is a gerbe over an algebraic space. If X is a gerbe, the fppf sheafification of isomorphism classes is an algebraic space (the base) and X is a gerbe over it. Gerbes are stable under base change and composition and descend along surjective flat lfp morphisms.

api.name: baseChange
api.statement: relativePullback: base changes of gerbes are gerbes.

api.name: comp
api.statement: relativeComposition: gerbes over gerbes are gerbes.

api.name: descent
api.statement: relativeDescent along surjective flat lfp Y' -> Y.

api.name: gerbeBase
api.statement: The base is SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.23's toModuliSheaf; it is unique and every map to an algebraic space factors through it.

api.name: equivalence
api.statement: Being a gerbe is invariant under equivalences.

tests.name: BG_gerbe
tests.statement: BG -> Spec k is a gerbe with base Spec k; an algebraic space is a gerbe over itself.

tests.name: A1Gm_not
tests.statement: [A^1/G_m] -> Spec k is not a gerbe: 0 and 1 are not locally isomorphic.

tests.name: pointToBG_not
tests.statement: Spec k -> BG (G nontrivial) is surjective and not a gerbe: automorphisms do not lift.

targets.name: Stacks.IsGerbeOver.classifyingEquiv
targets.statement: For a gerbe X -> U over an algebraic space with a section x and G = Isom(x,x), the canonical [U/G] -> X sending the trivial torsor to x is an equivalence, G -> U is flat lfp, and U -> X is surjective flat lfp.

tests.name: BG_identity
tests.statement: For BG with the trivial torsor the equivalence is the identity of BG.

tests.name: needs_gerbe
tests.statement: [A^1/G_m] with section 1: Isom trivial and Spec k is not [A^1/G_m].

tests.name: innerForm
tests.statement: For S_3 over R and a nontrivial torsor P, Isom(P,P) is the inner form, with B(Isom(P,P)) ≃ BS_3 sending the trivial torsor to P.

targets.name: Stacks.IsGerbeOver.flat_smooth
targets.statement: X -> Y is a gerbe iff after a surjective flat lfp U -> Y from an algebraic space it becomes [U/G] for a flat lfp group space G; gerbes are surjective, flat, lfp and smooth; [X/G] -> Y is smooth for X -> Y smooth and G flat lfp.
hypotheses: smoothness statement: X -> Y smooth morphism of algebraic spaces, G flat lfp acting over Y

tests.name: Bmup_smooth
tests.statement: B mu_p -> Spec F_p is smooth though mu_p is not; Spec F_p -> B mu_p is not smooth.

tests.name: BGm_baseChange
tests.statement: B G_m -> Spec Z is a gerbe with base change B G_{m,F_p}.

tests.name: flat_not_enough
tests.statement: Spec k -> B G_m is surjective flat lfp and not a gerbe.

targets.name: Stacks.isGerbe_iff_inertia_flat
targets.statement: An algebraic stack is a gerbe iff its inertia is flat and locally of finite presentation; for a gerbe X -> Y the relative inertia is flat lfp and the diagonal, the induced maps on fibre products and on Isom spaces are surjective flat lfp.
hypotheses: second part: X -> Y a gerbe

tests.name: A1Gm_inertia
tests.statement: [A^1/G_m] has non-flat inertia (G_m over 0, trivial over 1): not a gerbe.

tests.name: Bmup_gerbe
tests.statement: B mu_p has flat finitely presented inertia: a gerbe.

tests.name: free_action
tests.statement: A free action gives trivial inertia: [X/G] is an algebraic space (setoid_criterion).

targets.name: Stacks.isGerbeOver_iff_diagonal
targets.statement: X is a gerbe over Y iff f and its diagonal are surjective flat lfp; gerbes are universal homeomorphisms; quasi-compactness of the diagonal passes from X to Y.
hypotheses: f : X -> Y a morphism of algebraic stacks

tests.name: pointToBGm
tests.statement: Spec k -> B G_m: diagonal is the unit section of G_m, not flat.

tests.name: univHomeo_not_gerbe
tests.statement: Spec k -> Spec k[eps] is a universal homeomorphism, not a gerbe.

tests.name: BZ_diagonal
tests.statement: BZ -> Spec k is a gerbe; Spec k has qc diagonal but BZ does not.

targets.name: Stacks.denseOpenGerbe
targets.statement: A reduced algebraic stack with quasi-compact inertia has a dense open substack which is a gerbe, the largest open over which the inertia is flat lfp.

tests.name: A1Gm
tests.statement: On [A^1/G_m] the dense open gerbe is Spec k, the largest.

tests.name: example_29_2
tests.statement: On [Spec k[x0,x1,...]/G_m] with weights p^i the dense open gerbe is x0 != 0.

tests.name: needs_reduced
tests.statement: On [Spec k[eps]/G_m] the stabilizer Spec k[eps][l^±]/((l-1)eps) is not flat: no dense open gerbe; its reduction B G_m is a gerbe.

layers.title: Reduced one-point stacks and residual gerbes

targets.name: Stacks.isReducedSingleton_iff
targets.statement: If one field point is surjective flat, all are. Z is reduced with one point iff some Spec k -> Z is surjective flat, iff one is moreover locally of finite type; Z is reduced, locally Noetherian with one point iff some Spec k -> Z is surjective flat lfp.

tests.name: BG_singleton
tests.statement: B mu_p and B G_m are reduced, locally Noetherian, one-point.

tests.name: dualNumber
tests.statement: Spec k[eps] is one-point, not reduced; Spec k -> Spec k[eps] not flat.

tests.name: example_100_11_6
tests.statement: U/G (U = Spec(Qbar ⊗_Q Qbar), G = Gal(Qbar/Q) discrete) is reduced one-point and not locally Noetherian; Spec Qbar -> U/G is flat, surjective, lft and not lfp: Spec Qbar -> U is a closed immersion with non-finitely-generated ideal, flat because the local rings of U are Qbar.

targets.name: Stacks.monomorphism_rigidity
targets.statement: A monomorphism into a stack with a surjective flat lfp field point is empty or an equivalence; a reduced one-point stack contains a unique reduced locally Noetherian one-point substack, presented as [Spec k/R] for any surjective flat lft field point.
hypotheses: Spec k -> Z surjective flat lfp

tests.name: example_100_11_6
tests.statement: Spec Qbar -> U/G is a non-equivalence monomorphism; the core of U/G is Spec Qbar = [Spec Qbar/R] with R = Spec Qbar.

tests.name: needs_mono
tests.statement: Spec k -> BG is nonempty and not an equivalence.

tests.name: BG_core
tests.statement: For BG and Spec k the core is the whole stack.

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbe
targets.statement: For x in |X| the existence of a monomorphism from a one-point (reduced) stack onto x, or of a monomorphism with a surjective flat field point onto x, are equivalent, and then there is a unique reduced locally Noetherian one-point substack Z_x mapping to x: the residual gerbe.

api.name: mono
api.statement: Z_x -> X is a monomorphism with image {x} and a surjective flat lfp field point.

api.name: pointInvariant
api.statement: Existence and Z_x depend only on x; equivalences transport Z_x.

api.name: open
api.statement: For an open substack U containing x the residual gerbes of U and X coincide.

tests.name: scheme
tests.statement: For a scheme, Z_x = Spec kappa(x) with Mathlib Scheme.residueField.

tests.name: A1Gm
tests.statement: On [A^1/G_m], Z_0 = B G_m and Z_1 = Spec k; on BG, Z = BG.

tests.name: pointToBG_not
tests.statement: Spec k -> BG is not the residual gerbe: not a monomorphism.

tests.name: dualNumber
tests.statement: At the point of Spec k[eps] the residual gerbe is Spec k.

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbe_properties
targets.statement: When Z_x exists: it is regular; field points in the class x factor through it; monomorphisms from reduced locally Noetherian one-point stacks onto x are equivalences onto it; it inherits DM, quasi-DM, separated, quasi-separated; it is a gerbe over a reduced locally Noetherian one-point algebraic space (its base); along a gerbe X -> Y, Z_x = Z_y x_Y X; for algebraic spaces it is the residual space.
hypotheses: pullback clause: X -> Y a gerbe and Z_y existing

locator.where: Lemmas 100.11.10-100.11.12, Example 100.11.9, lines 1306-1337; stacks-06RD Lemma 101.4.16 lines 452-456, Lemma 101.51.1 lines 4831-4839; stacks-06QB Lemma 101.28.12 lines 2846-2861; stacks-decent-spaces lines 1500-1540

tests.name: singular_point
tests.statement: At the node of Spec k[x,y]/(xy) the residual gerbe Spec k is regular.

tests.name: base_not_field
tests.statement: Spec Q(t)/Z (Z acting by t -> t+1) is its own residual gerbe and not the spectrum of a field.

tests.name: A1Gm_base
tests.statement: Z_0 = B G_m on [A^1/G_m] is a gerbe over Spec k.

tests.name: pullback_needs_gerbe
tests.statement: For [A^1/G_m] -> Spec k the pullback of the residual gerbe of the base is the whole stack.

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbeMap
targets.statement: A morphism f with f(x) = y restricts to Z_x -> Z_y when both exist; if Spec k x_X Spec k -> Spec k x_Y Spec k is an isomorphism for one representative, Z_x -> Z_y is an isomorphism.

tests.name: pointToBG
tests.statement: Spec k -> BG gives Spec k -> BG, not an isomorphism; Spec k x_BG Spec k = G.

tests.name: openImmersion
tests.statement: Open immersions induce isomorphisms of residual gerbes.

tests.name: BG_to_point
tests.statement: BG -> Spec k induces BG -> Spec k, not an isomorphism.

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbe_finiteTypePoint
targets.statement: x is a finite type point iff some locally finite type map from a one-point stack has image x, iff Z_x exists and Z_x -> X is locally of finite type; for a closed point u of an affine smooth chart over x, Z_x = [u/(u x_X u)].

tests.name: A1Gm_open
tests.statement: Z_1 = Spec k -> [A^1/G_m] is an open immersion, locally of finite type.

tests.name: generic_not_ft
tests.statement: At the generic point of A^1_k the residual gerbe Spec k(t) exists and is not locally of finite type over A^1.

tests.name: Zp_generic
tests.statement: At the generic point of Spec Z_(p), Spec Q -> Spec Z_(p) is of finite type.

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbe_exists_of_flatQuasiFinitePresentation
targets.statement: If a scheme maps to X by a surjective, flat, lfp, locally quasi-finite morphism, residual gerbes exist at every point; in particular for algebraic spaces, Deligne-Mumford stacks and quasi-DM stacks.
hypotheses: U -> X surjective flat lfp locally quasi-finite from a scheme, or X an algebraic space, DM, or quasi-DM

locator.where: Lemma 101.31.2 and its proof, lines 3059-3095; stacks-decent-spaces Lemma 68.13.5 lines 1500-1531

tests.name: BZ2
tests.statement: B(Z/2) is DM and its residual gerbe is B(Z/2).

tests.name: Bmup

tests.name: A1QZ
tests.statement: On A^1_Q/Z residual spaces exist and at the generic point it is not the spectrum of a field.

tests.name: BGm_not_needed
tests.statement: B G_m is not quasi-DM and still has residual gerbes (4.3).

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbe_exists_of_gerbe_or_qcInertia
targets.statement: On a gerbe residual gerbes exist, Z_x = (X x_base Z_x^base)_red; with quasi-compact inertia residual gerbes exist, via the dense open gerbe of the reduced closure.
hypotheses: X a gerbe, or I_X -> X quasi-compact

tests.name: A1Gm
tests.statement: [A^1/G_m] has qc inertia, Z_0 = B G_m, Z_1 = Spec k (dense open gerbe).

tests.name: BZ

targets.name: Stacks.residualGerbe_exists_of_locallyNoetherian

tests.statement: Spec Q(t)/Z is locally Noetherian and is its own residual gerbe.

suppliers.what: Algebraic spaces and their points, group spaces, groupoids, stabilizers, torsors, Artin's bootstrap, stacks in groupoids, algebraic and DM stacks, inertia, SmoothLocal properties, |X|, quotient stacks, quasi-coherent modules and their description on a presentation (QCoh(BG) as comodules through QCoh.presentationEquiv), the moduli functor, generic flatness and regular schemes.
Gerbes and relative gerbes on a site with base change, composition and descent; framed deformation groupoids, deformation functors of points, the stabiliser action and framed tangent exact sequences.
Representations as comodules, Lie algebras and the smoothness criterion, quotients and orbits.

gaps.title: Permanence of morphism properties of algebraic stacks
gaps.detail: Stacks, Properties of Stacks, Lemmas 100.3.1-100.3.3, 100.5.2-100.5.5 (stacks-04XE lines 111-245, 577-590); Morphisms of Stacks, Lemmas 101.7.3-101.7.7, 101.7.10, 101.17.2-101.17.8, 101.25.2-101.25.5, 101.27.2-101.27.14, 101.27.16, 101.33.2-101.33.5 (stacks-06RD lines 801-889, 1478-1540, 2328-2357, 2438-2577, 3294-3308). SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 defines SmoothLocal and QuasiCompactStack with atlas independence only.
gaps.needs: SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 must prove, for its SmoothLocal properties (flat, lfp, lft, smooth), surjectivity and QuasiCompactStack, composition, base change, descent along surjective flat lfp base change, agreement with RepresentableProperty, the implications smooth => lfp => lft, cancellation for lft and lfp, and fppf-local essential surjectivity of surjective flat lfp morphisms.

gaps.title: Flat locally finitely presented morphisms of algebraic stacks are open
gaps.detail: Stacks, Morphisms of Stacks, Lemma 101.27.15 (stacks-06RD lines 2560-2567), used in the proof of Lemma 101.28.13 (stacks-06QB line 2875).
gaps.needs: SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 must prove that |f| is open for every flat, locally finitely presented morphism f of algebraic stacks.

gaps.title: Inertia is locally of finite type and pulls back to the stabilizer of a presentation
gaps.detail: Stacks, Morphisms of Stacks, Lemmas 101.5.1 and 101.5.7 (stacks-06RD lines 463-496, 609-618). SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 states inertia.representable only.
gaps.needs: SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 must prove that the inertia and relative inertia of algebraic stacks are locally of finite type and that the stabilizer of a presentation [U/R] ≃ X is U x_X I_X.

gaps.title: DM, quasi-DM and quasi-separated morphisms of algebraic stacks
gaps.detail: Stacks, Morphisms of Stacks, Definitions 101.4.1-101.4.2, Lemmas 101.4.3, 101.4.4, 101.4.10, 101.4.11, 101.6.1 (stacks-06RD lines 216-345, 637-657). DM stacks are SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19's IsDeligneMumford with .iff_unramified_diagonal.
gaps.needs: SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.20 must define DM, quasi-DM and quasi-separated morphisms and quasi-DM and quasi-separated stacks by the diagonal (DM stacks being §1.19's IsDeligneMumford), with their implications, base change, composition, Lemma 101.4.11 and the diagonal-inertia comparison Lemma 101.6.1.

gaps.title: Flat locally quasi-finite presentations of quasi-DM stacks
gaps.detail: Stacks, Morphisms of Stacks, Theorem 101.21.3 (stacks-06RD lines 1839-1842); §1.19 states the DM analogue Theorem 101.21.6.
gaps.needs: SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.19 must prove that an algebraic stack is quasi-DM iff it has a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented, locally quasi-finite morphism from a scheme.

gaps.title: Quotients of flat groupoids and the canonical comparison
gaps.detail: Stacks, Criteria for Representability, Theorem 97.17.2, Lemmas 97.17.1, 97.18.3 (stacks-criteria lines 1401-1424, 1509-1525); Groupoids in Spaces, Lemmas 78.25.1, 78.27.1-78.27.2; Algebraic Stacks, Lemma 94.16.1 and Remark 94.16.3.
gaps.needs: SchemeAndStackFoundations §1.21 must prove that for flat lfp groupoids in algebraic spaces [U/R] is algebraic and U -> [U/R] is surjective flat lfp, that [B/G] is algebraic iff G is flat lfp and is then a gerbe over B, that the canonical [U/R] -> X is fully faithful and an equivalence for surjective flat lfp U -> X, and that restricting a groupoid gives a fully faithful functor of quotients.

gaps.detail: Stacks, Decent Spaces, Definition 68.6.1, Lemmas 68.7.2, 68.8.3, 68.11.1, 68.15.2, Proposition 68.12.4 (stacks-decent-spaces lines 567-589, 710-716, 816-824, 1214-1220, 1364-1366, 1754).

gaps.detail: Stacks, Morphisms of Spaces, Proposition 67.32.1; Morphisms, Proposition 29.28.2 (used at stacks-06QB lines 2929-2932). §4.12 states generic_flatness for schemes over an integral base.

gaps.detail: Stacks, Descent, Lemmas 35.18.1, 35.18.4, 35.19.1-35.19.2; Descent on Spaces, Lemmas 74.9.2, 74.9.4; Spaces over Fields, Lemma 72.16.1 (cited at stacks-04XE lines 657-665 and stacks-06ML lines 1164-1166, 1314-1318).

gaps.detail: Stacks, Artin's Axioms, Lemma 98.5.2 and Section 98.8. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry §8.1 makes framed tangent spaces vector spaces under (RS) and states that algebraic stacks satisfy it without a target.
